neighbours.label: Returning to the same thing over and over: the point where 'again (and again)' is due ('the one I keep going back to', 'the same names come up', 'repeated'); a single visit or event stays quiet
fire: Among all my cookbooks there is one that I keep going back to, however many new ones I buy.
It is the film I find myself returning to, winter after winter.
There is a small beach on the island that we always come back to, summer after summer.
Whenever people argue about the best guitarists, the same handful of names come up.
Of all her poems, this is the one readers go back to, decade after decade.
A slogan sinks in when it is repeated day after day by every channel.
That is the question I keep coming back to, no matter how I try to avoid it.
He has one old sweater that he reaches for, morning after morning.
quiet: Among all my cookbooks there is one that I bought in Paris last spring.
It is the film I saw at the festival in March.
There is a small beach on the island that we found by accident.
People argued about the best guitarists at dinner on Friday.
Of all her poems, this is the one she wrote first.
The slogan was printed on a poster in the lobby.
That is the question I answered on the form yesterday.
He has one old sweater that his aunt knitted.

notes: Output promotes ' again' in many languages. Probes: 'keep coming back to,' 0.62, 'going back to,' 0.76, 'the same names always come up' 0.31, 'repeated over the years' 0.21, 'keep coming up' 0.19; open-ended 'made the same mistake' and 'she rebuilt it' near 0, so it is the going-back wording more than any slot for 'again'.
